questions.q: Which pillar is best suited to triggering an alert like 'page someone if error rate exceeds 5% for 5 minutes'?
options: Logs, because they contain the exact error message
Traces, because they show every span
Metrics, because they are cheap to store and fast to query on a threshold
None of the three can trigger alerts
questions.explain: Metrics are numeric and sampled regularly, making them cheap and fast to evaluate against a threshold — exactly what alerting needs.

questions.q: What is a 'span' in distributed tracing?
options: A dashboard panel showing a metric over time
One timed segment of a trace, representing work done in one service or operation
A log line with a severity level attached
The total duration of an incident
questions.explain: A trace is composed of spans — each span is a timed segment representing the work one service or operation did as part of the overall request.

questions.q: In the Northbridge flash-sale example, which pillar revealed WHERE in the request the delay was concentrated?
options: The metric dashboard
The trace, showing the slow span was the call to the pricing service
The log line
None of the pillars could show this
questions.explain: The trace broke the request into spans per service, revealing that the pricing-service span accounted for the bulk of the latency.

questions.q: Why can't metrics alone explain WHY checkout latency spiked?
options: Metrics are too expensive to collect during an incident
Metrics are numeric aggregates without the per-event detail needed to explain root cause
Metrics are only available after the incident ends
Metrics don't support dashboards
questions.explain: A metric tells you what and how much (e.g. latency is up), but it's an aggregate number — it doesn't carry the specific error message or request detail that explains why.

questions.q: What does 'correlation' mean in the context of the three pillars?
options: Storing metrics, logs, and traces in the same database
Using a shared identifier, like a trace ID, to move between a metric, a trace, and a log for the same incident
Running all three tools on the same server
Converting logs into metrics automatically
questions.explain: Correlation is the practice of linking signals across pillars using shared identifiers (like a trace ID) so you can move from 'something is wrong' to 'here is exactly why' quickly.
